adjudication_label: powder processing route comparison and phase formation
canonical_question: Does the 'excellent mechanical properties' and 'thermal stability' reported by Senkov et al. hold true when using mixed elemental powders instead of the pre-alloyed or vacuum AMF methods they used?

question_variants.question: Does the 'excellent mechanical properties' and 'thermal stability' reported by Senkov et al. hold true when using mixed elemental powders instead of the pre-alloyed or vacuum AMF methods they used?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The study confirms that mixed elemental powders can produce a HEA WTaMoNbV with a single-phase BCC structure and properties (strength, density, corrosion resistance) similar to the AMF counterpart, though defects like grain boundary segregation and printing defects remain due to non-optimized parameters and powder irregularity.

answers.answer: Samples produced by LPBF using mixed elemental powder achieved a single solid-phase solution with a BCC crystal structure similar to the AMF alloy. Mechanical testing showed higher compressive strength, density was similar, and corrosion resistance was outstanding and similar to the AMF alloy, though pitting corrosion showed an increased number of small pits.
answers.processing_state: Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) synthesized from mixed elemental powder
answers.conditions: Non-optimized printing parameters, inherent rapid solidification
answers.measurement_outcome: Compressive strength higher than AMF; density similar; corrosion resistance outstanding (similar to AMF); pitting increased compared to AMF.
answers.mechanism: V segregation at grain boundaries due to lower melting temperature compared to W; elemental inhomogeneity caused by irregular powder particle size.
answers.boundary_limitation: Printing parameters not optimized, leading to inherent printing defects; no post-heat-treatment performed.
evidence_spans: The attained results clearly demonstrated that the macrostructure and phase composition of samples produced by LPBF were similar to those obtained by its counterpart AMF alloy.
In both cases, the alloys were composed of a single solid-phase solution with a BCC crystal structure with similar lattice parameters, as expected according to Kang et al.
In terms of microstructure, both alloys showed differences in the distribution of tungsten and an increased amount of vanadium at grain boundaries.

source_evidence_spans: Their results demonstrated excellent mechanical properties and thermal stability at high temperatures (1200 °C).
